skills.pattern: a loop has a bound that is a function argument, struct field, or any non-compile-time constant, and Vitis HLS cannot determine the trip count
skills.strategy: Annotate any non-compile-time-bounded loop with `#pragma HLS loop_tripcount min=N avg=N max=N` so the synthesis report has a numeric latency estimate. Without this, latency comes back as 'undef' and the c2hls rubric scores 0 on M4 (Latency, 23% of total). On polybench kernels the upper bounds are tiny (40-100), so this is essentially free.
required_steps: scan the kernel for loops with non-constant bounds: `for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i)` where n is a parameter
for each such loop, find the actual maximum value (usually defined as a macro or constant in the header)
add `#pragma HLS loop_tripcount min=N avg=N max=N` immediately after the loop opening brace
use the max as a conservative estimate; the rubric scores based on the reported number
guards: loop_tripcount does NOT affect functional correctness — it only annotates for the scheduler/reporter
providing a tripcount that's smaller than the actual runtime trip count is safe (estimate vs actual)
if the loop runs at most N times statically, ALWAYS annotate it
